question.text: An insurance company wants to issue an investment-cum-insurance policy to a client. Under current regulations, which of the following is correct regarding suitability analysis?

answer.text: Suitability analysis is optional and at the discretion of the insurer
Suitability analysis is required only for policies with premium above Rs. 1,00,000
The insurer cannot issue the policy without conducting a suitability analysis; the agent may skip the requirement only with written consent from the policyholder
Suitability analysis is required only for ULIPs, not for other investment-cum-insurance products

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook page 37, insurance companies cannot issue an investment-cum-insurance policy until suitability analysis is done; agents may skip the requirement only with written consent from policyholders. Page 38 notes the relevance of the Investment Advisers Regulations for insurance-based security or investment products. The Trap: Option A treats the requirement as discretionary, contrary to page 37. Option B introduces a premium-based threshold that the source does not impose. Option D limits the rule to ULIPs even though the source applies it to investment-cum-insurance policies generally. Note: The written-consent exception is the only carve-out from the mandatory suitability-analysis requirement for these products.
